Zuberi, M.J.S., Hasanbeigi, A. and Morrow, W. (2022). Bottom-up assessment of industrial heat pump applications in U.S. Food manufacturing. Energy Conversion and Management 272, 116349. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enconman.2022.116349

Loaded: 11 heat-pump types by sink temperature (7 HTHP 54-90 degC hot water, 4 SGHP 107-150 degC steam) with the COP printed in Figs 4-12 (as %), sink temperature, state of development, and the common cost assumptions applied to every IHP (capex range read from Fig. 2, O&M 1%/yr, lifetime 15 yr, discount rate 10%); a reference natural-gas boiler (78% system efficiency, 0.05 tCO2/GJ); and for each of the nine food processes (Tables 1-9) the IHP electricity per t product and the conventional boiler fuel per t product. Not loaded (in _other-values): national heating capacities, production volumes, prices, emission factors, 2050 CO2 abatement-cost range across sectors (69-123 $/t), cost of conserved energy ($/GJ-saved, no parameter home; not a levelized cost of heat), savings totals. Not available: capacity factor (hours of operation used but not printed), levelized cost of heat, per-sector cost values (bar heights in Figs 15-18 only, not transcribed), per-process-step heat duties beyond the table totals.

(1) Capex is given only as a chart (Fig. 2) without equation or values; the loaded 450-950 range is a chart reading. (2) Several printed COPs do not match the stated method (45% x Carnot, 25 degC source): 54 degC printed 4.5 (method ~5.1), 63 degC printed 3.5 (~4.0), 107 degC printed 1.6 (~2.1); others match. (3) Table 4 total for IHP electricity is misprinted '33.6.6' (row value 336.6). (4) Table 7 (beet sugar) 'electricity use in other processes' column differs row-by-row from the conventional column and totals 36.5 vs 24.6 kWh/t, although only heat is said to change. (5) Table 9 modified 'direct & boiler fuel' total 4.4 GJ/t vs 1.9+2.4+0.2 = 4.5. (6) Conventional SECs and boiler efficiency are generic (Brown & Hamel 1996), not plant data; capacity factor/operating hours not printed. (7) Beet sugar production of '33 Mt of sugar' (Sec 3.1.6) is implausible for U.S. sugar output; likely beet input. (8) Conclusions paragraph says 'costs for electric boilers' though the study is about heat pumps.
